notes: kb/Work PB5242 landed. §1985:XIII.3.15.4 GR1: "A LINE NUMBER clause must be specified to establish each print line of a report group", and the 1985 clause is `integer-1 [ON NEXT PAGE]` or `PLUS integer-2` (§1985:XIII.3.15.2), so one clause establishes one line by an integer. The 2002 forms that break it are refused at 85: a LINE operand of NEXT PAGE with no integer (report-line-next-page-2002, VisitReportLineOperand) and the multiple LINE clause (report-multi-line-2002, VisitReportLineClause). Witnesses: 1985-GR-XIII_3_15_4-1 and pb5242-line-next-page-85. Each 2002 form is refused at --std 85 with COBOL0900 by a construct row of the version matrix (tests/version-matrix/constructs/report-*-2002.json, introducedIn 2002), checked on recognition in VersionConformancePass's parse arm, and accepted from COBOL-2002 (ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex F.2 item 115).

next.reason: 1985: 'A LINE NUMBER clause must be specified to establish each print line of a report group', so one clause establishes one print line. 2023 §2023:13.18.35.4 GR1 'Each LINE clause in a given report group description defines a report line, or set of report lines'; §2023:13.18.35.4 GR9 'A multiple LINE clause is functionally equivalent to a LINE clause with a single operand, together with a simple OCCURS clause'; §2023:13.15.4 GR3 a LINE entry with OCCURS or several operands is 'a repeating entry'. A report group whose single LINE clause establishes several print lines violates the 1985 requirement and is accepted by 2023: the restriction is lifted. Kept part: §2023:13.15.3 SR9 a COLUMN entry without LINE 'shall be subordinate to an entry with a LINE clause'.
